US Tariffs Hit Danish Oil & Gas Services & Equip Industry, Disrupting Exports and Operations

The Danish Oil & Gas Services & Equip industry is facing significant challenges following the United States’ imposition of a 20% tariff on imported oilfield equipment from Denmark. The measure, enacted earlier this month and currently in force, has led to immediate repercussions for Danish manufacturers and service providers, including Drilling Co of 1972 A/S/The.

Industry executives report a sharp slowdown in new orders and ongoing shipments bound for US clients. “The new tariffs have made our products significantly less competitive in the US market overnight,” said Jakob Pedersen, commercial director at the fictional NorthSea WellTech ApS. “We are already seeing cancellations and requests to renegotiate contracts.”

Drilling Co of 1972 A/S/The, which operates manufacturing facilities in Esbjerg and Aalborg, has confirmed it is reviewing staffing levels and production schedules in light of the reduced demand. “We are working closely with our workforce and union representatives to minimize the impact, but temporary layoffs cannot be ruled out if the situation persists,” a spokesperson said.

According to the Danish Oil & Gas Technology Association, the US accounted for approximately 18% of the industry’s export revenues last year. “This measure puts at risk hundreds of jobs and the viability of several sites that are heavily reliant on US business,” warned association chairperson Mette Lund. “We are urging swift engagement between the Danish and US governments to resolve the dispute.”

Analysts say the longer the tariffs remain in place, the greater the potential for lost market share to non-European competitors. Firms have begun exploring alternative markets, but industry sources note that diversification is challenging due to certification and compliance requirements.

For now, companies in Denmark’s Oil & Gas Services & Equip sector are bracing for further disruption as the trade-policy measure continues.
